hints: Use two pointers to locate the middle of the list.
Reverse the second half so its nodes are available from the end toward the middle.
Merge the two halves one node at a time, starting with the first half.
Be careful to break the first half before merging so the list does not form a cycle.
title: Reorder List Problem

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 5 * 10^4].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The list is split into two halves, the second half is reversed, and the two halves are merged alternately.
The last node is placed after the first, then the second-last after the second, and the middle node remains at the end.

content.problemStatement:
You receive the head of a singly linked-list. The list can be represented as:

```
L_0 → L_1 → … → L_n - 1 → L_n
```

*Reorder the list to be on the following form:*

```
L_0 → L_n → L_1 → L_n - 1 → L_2 → L_n - 2 → …
```

You may not modify the values in the list's nodes. Only nodes themselves may be changed.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/03/04/reorder1linked-list.jpg)

```
Input: head = [1,2,3,4]
Output: [1,4,2,3]
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/03/09/reorder2-linked-list.jpg)

```
Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5]
Output: [1,5,2,4,3]
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[1, 5 * 10^4]`.
* `1 <= Node.val <= 1000`

notes: The method mutates the linked list in place and returns no value.
The node values are never changed; only next pointers are rewired.
For odd-length lists, the middle node remains at the end after the merge.
solution.approach: Find the midpoint with slow and fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, then merge the two halves by alternating nodes.

better.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space
better.description: Use a stack to store all nodes from the second half, then traverse the first half and pop nodes from the stack to interleave them.

optimal.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space
optimal.description: Use slow/fast pointers to find the middle, reverse the second half in place, and merge the first half with the reversed second half alternately.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space
bruteForce.description: Store the nodes in an array, then reconnect them by taking one node from the front and one from the back repeatedly.

followUps: Can you reorder the list in O(1) extra space?
Why does the slow/fast pointer split work for both odd and even list lengths?
What changes if the list is allowed to contain zero nodes?
learningObjectives: Manipulate singly linked-list next pointers safely.
Use slow/fast pointers to find a list midpoint.
Reverse and merge linked-list segments in linear time with constant extra space.
